summary.headline: Technocraft Q4 FY26 margins lifted by a one-time INR20 crore steel quantity discount; management guides June quarter in line with Q4 but declines full-year outlook.
summary.overview: Management described a strong Q4 FY26, with scaffolding US demand recovering from the September quarter slowdown and sustained momentum into June. Scaffolding margin was boosted by a one-time INR20 crore steel quantity discount relating to prior quarters; the company cited the adjusted margin at about 16%. Forex gains of INR20 crore in Q4 (INR46 crore for FY26) also supported profitability. Aluminium formwork (Mach One) volumes were soft due to real estate project delays, though order book rose to over 4.5 lakh sq m. Management declined to give FY27 guidance beyond the June quarter, citing volatility.

segments.name: Scaffolding (US-led)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat QoQ but margin up sharply on INR20 crore one-time steel discount and higher volumes in US; FY26 scaffolding volumes down ~6.5% YoY per analyst, ~8% growth in division revenue cited. Middle East ~15% of FY26 scaffolding revenue; Europe ~1.5% after Poland B certificate.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork (Mach One)
segments.commentary: Volumes soft (down ~17% in Q4 per analyst); capacity utilisation ~60-70% due to slow site mobilisation; order book up QoQ to over 4.5 lakh sq m (>6 months of production). Extrusion plant at 100% utilisation. South America ~3% of formwork volume in FY26.

segments.name: Drum closures
segments.commentary: Stable demand and pricing; single-digit revenue growth; China growing strongly, rest of world ~4-5% growth in quantity and price. March quarter volumes down ~10 lakh sets YoY, which management attributed to a volatile prior-year base.

segments.name: Engineering services
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR80 crore per quarter, growing ~8-10% QoQ; investing heavily in AI-led services, which may cause bottom-line growth to lag top-line. Billing mainly headcount/hourly basis.

segments.name: Textiles (yarn and fabric)
segments.commentary: Yarn EBIT near breakeven, EBITDA ~10%; overall textile division still loss-making though losses narrowed in Q4. Fabric division under restructuring review; options include outsourcing processing and possible exit, not decided.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: No revenue update; samples under evaluation with DRDO and defence department; management declined to reaffirm earlier 5% to 10% of sales targets.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 segment projections, citing volatile geopolitical conditions and difficulty predicting quarters.
June quarter: scaffolding US momentum strong, driven by AI/tech infrastructure demand; margins expected to continue at similar levels.
Management expects 'a better year' than FY26 barring unforeseen events.
Scaffolding capacity up ~10-15% from debottlenecking in FY27; next formwork and extrusion expansion phase towards end of FY26 or early FY27 in Aurangabad, benefits in FY28-FY29.
Yarn margins expected to improve from Q1 FY27 on better yarn spreads; no incremental significant capex planned in Mach One this year.
capex_capacity: Scaffolding capacity up ~10-15% due to debottlenecking; some output increase expected in FY27.
Aluminium formwork: Mach One utilisation ~60-70%; extrusion plant at 100% utilisation; next expansion phase towards end FY26/early FY27.
Capex: FY26 maintenance/debottlenecking capex INR110 crore; management referenced ~INR150 crore for the next phase, not confirmed as a figure by management.
Plastic drum closure: no capacity addition needed; growth depends on customer acceptance of new specialised products.
Mach One extrusion plant entering second year of operation; recycling of own formwork gaining traction.
demand_pricing: US scaffolding demand recovered from Sep-quarter FY26 slump; sustained uptick since December 2025 per management; some summer seasonality possible in June-July.
Tariffs: scaffolding faces 50% under Section 232; drum closures 27.6%; China pays additional 25%. Management says tariffs fully passed through to customers.
Steel prices up ~25% in three months; passed through; aluminium costs passed through with variable pricing set at design approval.
Mach One competition intensifying with new capacity in India; management says it is not cutting prices, positioning as premium with backward integration.
Real estate developer delays (approvals, site readiness, funding) cited for Mach One offtake slowdown; inventories rose in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the scaffolding margin jump sustainable, and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR20 crore one-time steel discount; ex-one-time, margin improvement came from higher US volumes and better fixed-cost absorption. June quarter expected along similar lines; full-year not projected.

qa_highlights.question: Will engineering revenue reach INR120-130 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No; current run-rate is INR80 crore per quarter, growing 8-10% every quarter, so a jump to INR120 crore in one quarter is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex impact and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex gain was INR20 crore in Q4 and INR46 crore for FY26. Management said forex is recurring (positive or negative) since Technocraft has no imports and benefits from weaker rupee on exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to exit or restructure fabric or yarn?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric division restructuring under serious review, including possible outsourcing of processing; no decision on exit. Yarn EBITDA ~10%, EBIT breakeven due to ~INR46 crore depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the unallocated cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a mark-to-market reduction in the value of investments, booked in unallocated costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a defence revenue update?
qa_highlights.answer: No update; defence is in sample and approval stage with DRDO and defence department; no revenue targets reaffirmed.

risks_watch: Mach One volume weakness and receivable/inventory build from real estate developer delays; order book conversion pace.
One-time gains (INR20 crore steel discount) flatter Q4 margins; June quarter margin continuity is the key test.
Steel and aluminium price volatility and US tariff regime (Section 232) remain key cost and demand variables.
Textile division losses persist; fabric restructuring outcome and possible outsourcing decisions pending.
Defence and plastic closure product commercialisation timelines remain unclear; Europe demand still weak.
summary.management_tone: Confident on US scaffolding momentum and pricing pass-through, but notably cautious on full-year FY27 visibility and evasive on defence, fabric restructuring and FY27 margin guidance.
key_quotes: We are seeing a strong momentum even going forward into the June quarter across -- and this is mainly driven by investments in AI and tech ecosystem -driven infrastructure, which is leading to increased demand uptake of scaffolding.
There were some one -time benefits pertaining to quantity discounts that we obtained in this quarter for steel.
We are not -- we are a premium player. So we are not dropping our prices.
Ours is not an order book-driven business. We are in B2B business.
